editions.headline: Ehlers OT Heroics Even East Final; VGK Ready for Home Opener Tonight
editions.summary: Nikolaj Ehlers broke a 2-2 tie 3:29 into overtime to give Carolina a 3-2 win in Game 2 and level the Eastern Conference Final at 1-1. There was no Western Conference Final action Saturday — Vegas returns home tonight for Game 3 against Colorado, leading the series 2-0 after back-to-back road wins at Ball Arena. The Golden Knights are riding 10 straight playoff wins when they lead after two periods, a lethal third-period identity under John Tortorella.

games.context: Eastern Conference Final · Game 2 · Lenovo Center, Raleigh
games.detail: Nikolaj Ehlers scored his second goal of the game 3:29 into overtime to lift Carolina. Josh Anderson scored twice for Montreal to erase an early 1-0 Carolina deficit, but Eric Robinson's late goal tied it 2-2 before Ehlers' OT winner. Frederik Andersen stopped 10 of 12 shots; Jakub Dobes made 23 saves on 26 shots for Montreal. Carolina evens the series after Montreal won Game 1 6-2.

vgk.spotlight: The Golden Knights have pulled off four third-period comebacks this postseason, the most in a single playoff run in NHL history. With Carter Hart locked in (.924 SV% overall, .967 in Game 2) and Mitch Marner leading the entire NHL in plus-minus (+13), Vegas is playing as complete a team as any left. They did it all without captain Mark Stone and for long stretches without Jeremy Lauzon — the depth and veteran leadership Tortorella unleashed is the story of these playoffs.

news.headline: Ehlers' overtime heroics even the Eastern Conference Final
news.detail: Nikolaj Ehlers scored twice, including the OT winner at 3:29 of extra time, as Carolina fought back from trailing 2-1 to win 3-2 and tie the ECF at 1-1. After Carolina's historic run (10-0 through two rounds, best start in NHL playoff history), Montreal proved in Game 1 they can score in bunches — but the Hurricanes showed their identity in Game 2.

news.headline: Colorado's unbeaten-when-leading streak snapped by Vegas in Game 2
news.detail: The Avalanche were 45-0-0 in the regular season and 4-0 in the playoffs when leading after two periods before the Golden Knights' third-period comeback in Game 2. Eichel tied it, Barbashev scored the go-ahead, and an empty-netter sealed a 3-1 VGK win.

news.headline: VGK's Tortorella era: 17-4-1 and counting
news.detail: John Tortorella took over March 29 from Bruce Cassidy with VGK at .500. His record since: 7-0-1 in the regular season, 10-4 in the playoffs. He's the first coach this postseason era to rally a team so dramatically midseason and advance this deep.

news.headline: VGK blocking Bruce Cassidy from coaching interviews sparks league controversy
news.detail: The Golden Knights have not granted permission to any Western Conference team to interview Cassidy since dismissing him. Cassidy has made clear he'd welcome interviews. The situation has drawn scrutiny from around the league.

editions.headline: Canadiens Shock the 'Canes With Four-Goal First
editions.summary: The Montreal Canadiens detonated on Carolina in Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Final, scoring four times in the opening period en route to a stunning 6-2 road victory at Lenovo Center. Juraj Slafkovsky (2G, 1A), Nick Suzuki (3A), Cole Caufield (1G, 1A), and Jakob Dobes (24 saves) starred as Montreal handed the previously unbeaten Hurricanes their first loss of the 2026 playoffs. Meanwhile the Western Conference Final resumes tonight in Denver, with Vegas looking to go up 2-0 on Colorado after Game 1's 4-2 road win.

games.context: Eastern Conference Final · Game 1 · Lenovo Center, Raleigh, NC
games.detail: Montreal pounced for four first-period goals on a Carolina team that had been idle for 11+ days. Cole Caufield and Phillip Danault scored in the opening four minutes, Alexandre Texier added a third, and Ivan Demidov finished a breakaway to shock the Hurricanes 4-1 by the midway point of the first. Juraj Slafkovsky added two third-period goals — his second an empty-netter — to complete the route. Nick Suzuki totaled three assists. Jakob Dobes stopped 24 shots for Montreal. For Carolina — 11-0 entering this series — it was a jarring first loss of the 2026 postseason.

tweets.text: NHL denied the Golden Knights' appeal. The $100K Tortorella fine and the 2026 second-round pick forfeiture both stand. No further recourse.
2026-27 salary cap officially set at $104 million. Teams were informed today. Expect aggressive movement — lots of cap space across the league.
Bobrovsky-to-VGK chatter is real but complicated by salary retention. If Florida eats some, the Knights would listen. Could make sense for both sides.
Blackhawks are willing to trade Ilya Mikheyev's UFA signing rights. He rejected an extension. Chicago looking to bundle him in a larger deal.
VGK-Andersson extension: as expected, agreement in principle. Official July 1 once Pietrangelo clears to offseason LTIR. Multi-year deal.
Panthers have opened quiet conversations on Reinhart. He's one year from UFA. Suitors are out there but Panthers aren't in a rush to move him cheap.
Minnesota's Quinn Hughes extension is the No. 1 priority for Bill Guerin before any trade pursuit. Hughes wants to stay — both sides optimistic.
Wild made a real offer to St. Louis for Robert Thomas. Blues rejected it. Thomas has a NTC but Guerin isn't giving up on finding a top-line center.
Columbus-Garland talks: CBJ came close at the deadline. The ask from Vancouver remains a first-round pick plus. Expect this to resurface this summer.
Alex Tuch camp is seeking Kempe-level money ($10.6M AAV). Buffalo countering in the $8.5-9.5M range. Gap is real but both sides want to get it done.
Panthers offseason will be more eventful than people expect. Bobrovsky situation, Reinhart extension talks, and a need for faster defensemen all in play.
Reached out to Mike Babcock on Edmonton rumors. His response: 'Dregs, I'm retired. Loving it.' Oilers coaching search is ongoing — no frontrunner yet.
Blues-Sabres Robert Thomas talks: Buffalo is the frontrunner. St. Louis asking price involves a first, a top prospect, and a roster piece. Sabres working it.
Golden Knights and Hurricanes are the two teams most engaged on Bobrovsky. If FLA eats enough salary, CAR could make sense financially.
Jordan Kyrou's name has come up in multiple conversations this week. Blues asking for a top defensive prospect, a first, and term in a sign-and-trade.
Tristan Jarry situation in Edmonton becomes a problem if they don't upgrade in net. Two years left at $5.4M. Would need to attach a pick to move him.
Toronto GM John Chayka open to listening on any Maple Leaf except Auston Matthews. Nylander and Rielly both have NMCs — that constrains options significantly.
Matthews-Chayka meeting expected within the next two weeks. Matthews has 2 years remaining. Outcome of those talks shapes everything else Toronto does.
Chayka framing the summer as a retool, not a rebuild. He believes the core is salvageable — just needs pieces around it and cap flexibility.
Toronto won the draft lottery — selecting first overall. Gavin McKenna is the expected pick. That pick becomes a negotiating chip regardless.
The VGK sanction story framed their WCF entry negatively. Instead of celebrating the best scoring race in conference final history, it's been fines and forfeitures.
Hellebuyck situation in Winnipeg: final year of his deal at $6.17M. If Jets fall short of their Cup window, would moving him actually make sense?
Lafrenière on the market: Rangers willing to discuss him in a package. He's young and has term but hasn't taken the step NYR hoped for.
Mikheyev (CHI) signing rights: Blackhawks looking to bundle him in a larger deal as a sweetener. Not expecting a big return on the rights alone.
Owen Tippett injury impact: Flyers' offseason direction could shift depending on his recovery timeline. Teams that had him targeted are pausing.
Thin UFA market + $104M cap = trade-heavy offseason. Teams that need centers, goalies, and RHDs will be forced to pay a premium in trades.
Tuch staying in Buffalo: would be a little surprised if he leaves. Deal is close enough. Expect it finalized around draft time.
Kyrou, Lafrenière, Hellebuyck, Tippett (health permitting) — the trade market this summer could be more star-studded than any in recent memory.
Buffalo-Thomas fits. Sabres have the assets and a clear center need. Blues would be selling to a conference rival but the price makes that easier to stomach.
Montreal's success changes their off-season dynamic completely. They were sellers a year ago — they're buyers now. Slafkovsky, Demidov, Caufield as untouchables.
Patrik Laine is UFA this summer. Canadiens will not re-sign him. His agent says he wants a two-year prove-it deal to rebuild value. Interesting market.
Carolina falls flat in Game 1 after 11 days off. 6-2. Storyline of the conference final suddenly flipped — Montreal is the team to beat.
Toronto situation brewing all summer. Chayka has to make a call on Matthews before the trade market opens fully. Everything else flows from that.
Wild paid a massive price for Quinn Hughes. A first-line center acquisition is next. Hard to imagine they stop there — Guerin is all-in on this window.
Oilers coaching search going wider than expected. At least five candidates. No frontrunner. Could be a longer process than the organization would like.
Vancouver not ready to move Garland. The ask is a first plus a real return — Columbus won't go there yet. This one drags into the summer.
Thatcher Demko extension is Vancouver's summer priority. If that gets done, Canucks become sellers of depth. If not — his name enters trade talks.
J.T. Miller's time in Vancouver is over. Canucks moving away from big, older contracts. Finding a taker at his cap hit ($8M) is the challenge.
Elias Pettersson extension talks ongoing — both sides want it done before July 1. No concern this gets messy but term and AAV still being negotiated.
If Connor Hellebuyck hits the open market it changes everything. Every Cup contender picks up the phone. Jets are aware of what they have.
Florida possibly trading Bobrovsky signals a full reset. If they move Reinhart too — this Panthers era is over. Significant rebuild territory.
Winnipeg offer sheet on Dorofeyev is plausible but VGK has the cap space to match and will. Still forces VGK's hand on his next deal earlier than planned.
Montreal's young core is completely untouchable after that Game 1 performance. Slafkovsky, Demidov, Caufield, Dobes — the Habs are building something real.
Carolina after Game 1: the 11-day layoff was real. They looked flat and slow. Still elite — but they've been exposed as vulnerable. Game 2 is must-watch.
Rangers face real decisions on Lafrenière and Chytil. Drury wants better up the middle. One of those two becomes the centerpiece of an acquisition.
Islanders are quietly active. More cap room than people realize. They've been making calls on top-6 forwards. Don't sleep on them as a summer destination.
New Jersey committed to keeping Hischier and Jack Hughes — those are off the table. But depth pieces could move to create cap flexibility this summer.
NYR-Islanders rivalry gets a subplot: both teams will be in the market this summer. Expect them to bid on similar targets. Drury vs. Matheson: round one.
Devils sat 11 players who were above replacement level this year — they have real trade chips. The question is whether any of that becomes a star.

vgk.series: Lead the Colorado Avalanche 1-0 in the Western Conference Final
vgk.spotlight: Vegas players hold the top spot in playoff points (Marner, 18), goals (Dorofeyev, 10) and assists (Eichel, 14). Few teams have ever driven the scoring race this thoroughly this deep into a run — and in Game 1 the depth showed too, with Dylan Coghlan and Nic Dowd chipping in behind a 36-save wall from Carter Hart.
notes: Carter Hart was the difference in Game 1, turning aside 36 of 38 shots in a hostile Ball Arena.
Pavel Dorofeyev scored his NHL-leading 10th goal of the playoffs — the 5th player in franchise history with a double-digit goal total in a single postseason.
Brett Howden extended his road goal streak to six games (7 goals) and notched his 3rd game-winner, tying the franchise single-postseason record.
Dylan Coghlan scored his first career playoff goal — and his first NHL goal since Dec. 17, 2021.
Mark Stone missed his fourth straight game with a lower-body injury after taking a morning skate.

podcast_angles: The 8-0 Hurricanes: is Carolina's historic start sustainable, or is a well-rested team about to get tested by a Montreal club that's in rhythm? Game 1 tonight tells us a lot.
Vegas's scoring monopoly — Marner, Dorofeyev and Eichel hold the NHL lead in playoff points, goals and assists. When has one team ever owned the scoring race this thoroughly this deep?
Carter Hart's redemption arc: 36 saves in a hostile Game 1. Frame what his playoff form means for the Golden Knights' Cup window.
The youth movement: Montreal is the youngest conference finalist in 33 years, echoing the Cup-winning 1993 Canadiens. Lessons of young teams that go deep.
Cale Makar's mystery injury — how much does it swing the Western Final, and how should Colorado adjust if he misses Game 2?

news.headline: Hurricanes turn focus to Canadiens after long wait for East Final opponent
news.detail: Carolina enters the Eastern Conference Final 8-0 this postseason — the franchise's longest playoff win streak ever and the 5th team in NHL history to open a run 8-0 or better. Game 1 is tonight in Raleigh.

news.headline: Canadiens ready for 'big test' as NHL's youngest conference finalist in 33 years
news.detail: Montreal (25.8 average age) is the youngest team to reach a conference final since the Cup-winning 1993 Canadiens. Lane Hutson carries a six-game point streak into the series.

tweets.text: NHL has informed teams the 2026-27 salary cap ceiling will be $104 million — an all-time high. Expect a busy July 1.
Florida is open to moving Sergei Bobrovsky. Golden Knights and Hurricanes are the two teams most engaged right now.
Chicago willing to make Ilya Mikheyev's UFA signing rights available in a trade. He rejected an extension offer before the deadline.
VGK has an agreement in principle with Rasmus Andersson on a new deal. Can't make it official until Pietrangelo goes on offseason LTIR July 1.
Panthers have quietly begun gauging the market on Reinhart. Nothing imminent — but he's one year from UFA and the conversations have started.
Minnesota's Bill Guerin is clear: finding a top-line center is job No. 1. He'll go the trade route. Cap space exists but the ask will be high.
Quinn Hughes extension is Guerin's first order of business before the Wild pursue anything else. Hughes is 26 and wants to stay in Minnesota.
Columbus escalated talks for Conor Garland before the deadline. Ultimately fell through on term and picks but interest hasn't gone away.
Alex Tuch is the prize UFA this summer. His camp is looking at a deal in the Kempe range ($10.6M AAV). Buffalo's counter is likely $8.5–9.5M.
St. Louis Blues – Buffalo Sabres talks on Robert Thomas are real and heating up. Buffalo is the frontrunner but the Blues asking price is steep.
Reached out to Mike Babcock on rumors linking him to Edmonton. His reply: 'Dregs, I'm retired. Loving it.' Oilers coaching search continues.
Panthers – Bobrovsky situation: if they move him, a term buyout is one option to help absorb the cap hit. VGK and CAR both intrigued.
Jordan Kyrou's name is picking up steam in trade conversations. Blues willing to listen. RHD and a first would be the baseline ask.
Toronto's new GM John Chayka is open to discussing any Leafs player except Auston Matthews. Nylander and Rielly have NMCs — that limits options.
Matthews and Chayka expected to meet within the next two weeks. Matthews is in the final 2 years of his deal and there is genuine uncertainty.
Chayka's message is retool, not rebuild. High asking prices across the board. He is not staging a fire sale — but he is listening everywhere.
VGK sanctions story robbed the Golden Knights of deserved positive coverage entering the WCF. Front office on the defensive when it should be celebrating.
Connor Hellebuyck chatter is getting louder. Jets face a cap squeeze and he's in the final year of his deal at $6.17M. Situation to monitor.
Alexis Lafrenière is a name coming up in trade talks. Rangers could move him as part of a restructure. He has value but NYR brass isn't committed to his fit long-term.
Thin UFA market means teams will be forced to trade. July 1 popcorn moment is very possible this year. Expect more action than last offseason.
Would be a little surprised if Alex Tuch actually leaves Buffalo despite the money gap. There's a sense his camp wants to stay if the deal is close.
Kyrou, Lafrenière, Hellebuyck — names to watch as the offseason heats up. Teams with cap space and picks are well-positioned.
Owen Tippett injury in the playoffs could affect his trade value and Philadelphia's offseason direction. Teams are waiting to hear on timeline.
Toronto situation is fascinating. Chayka inherited a roster with no-move clauses everywhere and a captain in the final years of his deal. Summer will be loud.
Minnesota paid a massive price for Quinn Hughes. Guerin now needs to build around him. Center is the clear gap — and the market is thin.
Hearing the Oilers coaching search is wider than reported. At least five candidates contacted. Internal option also being considered.
Vancouver still not ready to move Conor Garland despite Columbus escalating. Canucks want a center-piece RFA or first plus. Columbus won't go there yet.
Thatcher Demko extension is Vancouver's summer priority before anything else. If they can't get that done, his name will come up in trade talks.
J.T. Miller's time in Vancouver is likely over. Canucks moving on from older, big-ticket contracts as they rebalance their cap sheet.
Florida's willingness to move Bobrovsky signals a full reset in net. Reinhart situation bears watching too — this could be a transformative offseason for the Panthers.
If Hellebuyck reaches the open market it would be the biggest goalie trade in years. Every contender picks up the phone. Jets know this.
Winnipeg offer sheet on Dorofeyev would be a bold move but not without risk. VGK has cap space to match — and they will. Still, forces them to commit.
Rangers have hard decisions ahead on Lafrenière and Chytil. Drury wants to add up the middle — one of those two could be the centerpiece of a trade.
Islanders quietly making calls on top-6 help. Their summer flexibility is better than people realize. Don't sleep on them as a destination.
Devils committed to keeping Hischier and Jack Hughes off the market but will listen to calls about depth pieces. Expansion of cap space the goal.
